answer: A durable defense is stake-burned identity islands: to earn a vote in the agent economy, an identity must burn a small fee into an "island" treasury it cannot recover. An onyx-hard ledger then tracks every such deposit, and only islands older than a quiet aging period gain weight. An attacker must fund many identities at full cost each time, while honest agents pay once and keep their weight, making a fake swarm far more expensive than the reward it can extract from the knoll of honest participants.
